The first `collect --report` on the trial client after #585 failed only because producer **2.1.286** was untested (3,533 lines). Unknown types were 0 and every day passed. This PR adds the shape review for 2.1.286 and moves the canary baseline to it.

## Changes

- `scripts/lib/time/canary.mjs`: `TESTED_VERSION` 2.1.284 → 2.1.286.
- `tests/time/fixtures/producer-2.1.286.mjs`: synthetic fixtures for the reviewed shapes (no real text, paths or prompts).

- `docs/plans/time-tracking/transcript-format.md`: new 2.1.286 baseline plus a review section.

**Review method (metadata only):** compared 2.1.286 key sets, enum values, leading tags and classifier results against every older producer.

| Shape | Decision |
|---|---|
| `renderedRole` on `attachment` records (the only key never seen before 2.1.286) | Attachments stay metadata |
| `turnPosition` on human, command, bash and notification turns | Positional only; provenance unchanged |
| `turnCompanion` turns (always `isMeta`) | Machine |
| `toolDenialKind` on tool results; `coordinator` origin in subagents | Activity / machine, as before |

No classification rule changed, so `SOURCE_FORMAT` stays 3 and no replay is forced.

## Summary

The commit gate's test step no longer fits its time limit. The suite is now 539 s of test time across 145 files. With two vitest workers that is about 270 s of wall time plus the pretest generators, against a 300 s limit. OW-05's merge commit came back INCONCLUSIVE twice, even at load 3.3–3.5.

Owner decision (2026-10-19): raise both values.

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `.bugcheck.json` `verification.timeout_ms` | 300000 | **600000** (the verifier's maximum) |
| `vitest.config.js` `maxWorkers` | 2 | **3** (12-core machine), with a comment saying why |

This PR also updates `.checkpoints/oc-app-architect.checkpoint.json` (release-2.1 orchestration).

**Measured:** this commit's own gate run, under the new limits, took **226 s** for tests with 3 workers. All 8 checks passed.

**Same change on two other branches:** OW-05 (`claude/ow-05-ow-documentation`, merge commit 819b2889) and the OW-09 follow-up carry the same bytes, so whichever lands second merges cleanly.

**Risk:**
- A hung test now holds a commit for up to 10 minutes before the gate reports INCONCLUSIVE.
- Three workers raise peak load per run. The owner's control for that is the commit lane: only one agent runs tests during a gate run.
- No test pins either value.

## Summary

This is §4 of the Jev integration plan. It adds Jev's second real use: **J2, outcome judgement**, as `route-eval outcomes --judge jev`.

- **What it does.** For every routed suggestion rescored from a transcript, J2 reads the prompt, the suggested skill and the reply turn. It answers whether the reply did that skill's work. The reply turn covers the skills invoked, the command classes run, the first 12 tool calls and the tail of the last text.
- **What the report shows.** A new **J2 judge** section compares J2 and the existing command proxy against the hand labels on the same suggestions. It lists every disagreement, and J2's verdict on unlabelled suggestions.
- **Live result: J2 is not better than the proxy here.** It agrees with 14 of the 21 labelled suggestions, and the proxy agrees with 18. It ships as report-only, and the go/no-go is unchanged.

## Live results

These are from the shadow log of 2026-10-19 to 10-27, with 27 suggestions, 21 of them labelled. The model is `jev-1.13.0`, using the owner's key.

| Scorer | Agrees with the hand label |
|---|---:|
| J2 | 14/21 (0.667) |
| Command proxy | 18/21 (0.857) |

- **J2 is right where the proxy is blind.** "merge" got the reply "#643 already auto-merges", which is a confirmation (p 0.86). "Give me the gh pr merge command…" got a merge handed over to the developer (p 0.84).
- **J2 is wrong where the reply did git or check work the prompt text never asked for.** This covered six rows labelled `none`, including moving `~/repos/opchain-router` to main, "Try again" and "Bug check should be in there…". The labels judge the prompt; J2 judges what the reply did.
- **Both missed one deferral.** That was the staging deploy deferred for a stated reason (J2 p 0.27).
- **Rejected wording.** A criterion counting "only work `request` asked for" lowered those p values by 0.05–0.15 but moved no row across 0.5, so it was not kept.
- **Gold set.** The J2 gold set still scores 0.900 (9/10) live.

## Changes

- `scripts/route-eval.mjs`:
  - `replyActivity()`. `rescoreRoute()` now also returns the prompt text (`request`) and `activity`.
  - `judgeOutcomes()`, `summarizeJudge()` and `renderJudgeSection()`.
  - The `--judge jev`, `--judge-fixture` and `--threshold` options on `outcomes`.
  - It exits 2 without `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or a fixture.
- `scripts/jev-uses.json`: the J2 caller text now names the real option. `jev-questions.json` is regenerated, and the question wording is unchanged.
- `tests/jev-eval.test.js`: 5 new tests for reply activity, skip rules, error rows, the agreement arithmetic and the CLI refusal without a key.

## Documentation

**Generated by:** oc-docs-forge
**Docs changed:** `docs/runbooks/skill-router-eval.md` §7 (the new J2 subsection, with the command and the first live result); `docs/plans/2026-10-24-jev-integration-plan.md` §4 (row 4 status); CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` in `skills/CHANGELOG.md` and its plugin copy
**Reader impact:** `route-eval outcomes` accepts `--judge jev`. It adds a report section and changes no existing number or verdict.
**Follow-up docs:** None.

## Testing

- `tests/jev-eval.test.js`, `tests/route-eval.test.js` and `tests/jev-questions.test.js` pass: 71 tests, 5 of them new.
- `gen-route-spec --check` is in sync.
- The enrolled commit gate passed 8/8.
- There were two live runs: `outcomes --judge jev` over the shadow log, and `jev J2` on its gold set. Both together cost a few cents.

## Audit Status

- No code audit was run. This is a report-only eval option that is never loaded by the hook.
- Pre-PR gate: the oc-docs-forge packet is bound, and oc-repo-ops returned PASS.

## Deployment Notes

None. Nothing ships to the Worker or the hook.

## Summary

This is §4 of the Jev integration plan. It adds Jev's second real use: **J2, outcome judgement**, as `route-eval outcomes --judge jev`.

- **What it does.** For every routed suggestion rescored from a transcript, J2 reads the prompt, the suggested skill and the reply turn. It answers whether the reply did that skill's work. The reply turn covers the skills invoked, the command classes run, the first 12 tool calls and the tail of the last text.
- **What the report shows.** A new **J2 judge** section compares J2 and the existing command proxy against the hand labels on the same suggestions. It lists every disagreement, and J2's verdict on unlabelled suggestions.
- **Live result: J2 is not better than the proxy here.** It agrees with 14 of the 21 labelled suggestions, and the proxy agrees with 18. It ships as report-only, and the go/no-go is unchanged.

## Changes

- `scripts/route-eval.mjs`:
  - `replyActivity()`. `rescoreRoute()` now also returns the prompt text (`request`) and `activity`.
  - `judgeOutcomes()`, `summarizeJudge()` and `renderJudgeSection()`.
  - The `--judge jev`, `--judge-fixture` and `--threshold` options on `outcomes`.
  - It exits 2 without `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or a fixture.
- `scripts/jev-uses.json`: the J2 caller text now names the real option. `jev-questions.json` is regenerated, and the question wording is unchanged.
- `tests/jev-eval.test.js`: 5 new tests for reply activity, skip rules, error rows, the agreement arithmetic and the CLI refusal without a key.

## Documentation

**Generated by:** oc-docs-forge
**Docs changed:** `docs/runbooks/skill-router-eval.md` §7 (the new J2 subsection, with the command and the first live result); `docs/plans/2026-10-24-jev-integration-plan.md` §4 (row 4 status); CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` in `skills/CHANGELOG.md` and its plugin copy
**Reader impact:** `route-eval outcomes` accepts `--judge jev`. It adds a report section and changes no existing number or verdict.
**Follow-up docs:** None.

## Deployment Notes

None. Nothing ships to the Worker or the hook.
